title: Lakshmir Bhandar 2026: Amount, Status, Eligibility
meta_description: Lakshmir Bhandar 2026: ₹1,500/month (general), ₹1,700 (SC/ST) for WB women aged 25-60. Status check, eligibility, and the Annapurna Bhandar transition.

hero.one_liner: West Bengal's monthly cash support for women aged 25-60. Currently ₹1,500 general and ₹1,700 for SC/ST, with the Annapurna Bhandar transition underway.

what_is_it: Lakshmir Bhandar is a West Bengal scheme that pays a monthly cash allowance to women household members aged 25 to 60. It is run by the state Women and Child Development department.
As of 2026 the amount is ₹1,500 a month for general category women and ₹1,700 for SC/ST women, after a ₹500 rise in the February 2026 budget. The money is paid by direct transfer.

extra_sections.title: Lakshmir Bhandar Has Been Replaced by Annapurna Bhandar
extra_sections.content:
As of June 1/3, 2026, Lakshmir Bhandar has been replaced by the Annapurna Bhandar scheme (also called Annapurna Yojana). The new scheme pays ₹3,000 per month to all eligible women - up from ₹1,700 (SC/ST) and ₹1,500 (General) under the old scheme.

Existing Lakshmir Bhandar beneficiaries are being automatically migrated. However, an audit removed approximately 30 lakh beneficiaries who were found ineligible.

If your payment stopped around June 2026, your account may have been flagged during the audit. Read the migration and eligibility sections below to understand what to do.

extra_sections.heading: What Was Lakshmir Bhandar and Why It Changed
content: Lakshmir Bhandar was the West Bengal government's flagship monthly cash transfer scheme for women. Launched in 2021, it paid ₹1,000 per month to General category women and ₹1,200 per month to SC/ST women from households headed by women.
The amounts were subsequently revised upward to ₹1,500 and ₹1,700 respectively. At its peak, approximately 2.2 crore women were enrolled.

The scheme was a major political and welfare landmark for West Bengal. It was one of the larger women-targeted direct benefit transfer programmes in any Indian state, and its implementation was credited with a significant increase in women's financial independence in rural and semi-urban Bengal.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 What Was Lakshmir Bhandar and Why It Changed (more)
content: In 2026, following a change in the state's political landscape, the incoming government rebranded and restructured the scheme. The renamed scheme - Annapurna Bhandar (also referred to as Annapurna Yojana or Matri Shakti Bharosa Scheme in early announcements) - offers a flat ₹3,000 per month to all eligible women regardless of category.
The SC/ST and General category distinction in the payment amount was removed.
The transition from Lakshmir Bhandar to Annapurna Bhandar was not just a renaming. It included a fresh eligibility audit of the existing 2.2 crore beneficiaries.

The audit identified approximately 30 lakh beneficiaries who were deemed ineligible - primarily government employees, income tax payers, pensioners, and those whose Aadhaar-linked bank details were outdated or invalid. These beneficiaries were removed from the list.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 What Was Lakshmir Bhandar and Why It Changed (continued)
content: The remaining approximately 2 crore existing Lakshmir Bhandar beneficiaries were auto-migrated to Annapurna Bhandar, with their ₹3,000 payments beginning from June 2026. No fresh application was needed for existing, verified beneficiaries.
However, new applicants who were not previously on Lakshmir Bhandar must apply fresh during the 90-day enrollment window that runs until August 25, 2026.

For women who were on Lakshmir Bhandar but were removed during the audit: the government has announced an appeal or review process. If you believe you were incorrectly removed - for example, because your job ended before June 2026 or because the government employee link in your database record is wrong - you should file an objection through the portal or in person at your local BSK or gram panchayat.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 What Was Lakshmir Bhandar and Why It Changed (more 2)
content: The name 'Lakshmir Bhandar' will continue to be used in everyday conversation for years, much as the old name persists even after official renaming. For status checks, the official portal socialsecurity.wb.gov.in continues to serve both old Lakshmir Bhandar records and the new Annapurna Bhandar scheme.

The scale of this transition is significant. Moving 2.2 crore women from one scheme to another while simultaneously conducting an eligibility audit and increasing the payment amount by ₹1,300-1,500 per person represents one of the larger welfare scheme transitions seen in any Indian state.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 What Was Lakshmir Bhandar and Why It Changed (part 2)
content: The implementation challenge - ensuring existing beneficiaries receive their enhanced payments without interruption while filtering out ineligible entries - is administratively complex. Minor delays in individual payments during this transition period are therefore expected.

The socialsecurity.wb.gov.in portal may experience high traffic around payment dates and after major announcements about the scheme. If the portal is slow or returns an error when you try to check status, try again at a different time - early morning or late evening typically has lower load.
Alternatively, BSK centres and gram panchayat offices can check your status using their official access even when the public portal is slow.

One practical point that many beneficiaries miss: the payment date each month may shift slightly during the transition. Under Lakshmir Bhandar, most beneficiaries received their payment around a consistent date each month.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 What Was Lakshmir Bhandar and Why It Changed (more 3)
content: Under Annapurna Bhandar, the payment schedule for June-August 2026 may be irregular as the new system stabilises. Track your bank account and the portal rather than relying on a fixed expected date.

Households where the woman recently turned 60 should note that the scheme stops at 60. If you received Lakshmir Bhandar past your 60th birthday (which sometimes happened due to age verification lapses in the original enrollment), Annapurna Bhandar will not include you.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 What Was Lakshmir Bhandar and Why It Changed (part 3)
content: However, you may apply for the Old Age Allowance, which is a separate scheme administered by the Social Welfare Department for women above 60 who meet the income criteria.

extra_sections.heading: How to Check Lakshmir Bhandar / Annapurna Bhandar Status 2026

steps.title: Go to the official portal
steps.description:
Visit socialsecurity.wb.gov.in. This portal serves both the old Lakshmir Bhandar records and the new Annapurna Bhandar scheme.

Do not use unofficial third-party websites that promise status checks - they cannot access the actual government database and many are designed to collect personal information.

steps.title: Click 'Track Applicant Status'
steps.description: On the homepage, find the Track Applicant Status or Status Check option. This may be labelled under Annapurna Bhandar or may still show the old Lakshmir Bhandar label during the transition period.

steps.title: Enter your mobile number and CAPTCHA
steps.description:
Enter the mobile number that was registered with your Lakshmir Bhandar or Annapurna Bhandar application. Complete the CAPTCHA security check and click Submit.

If your mobile number is not linked, try entering your Aadhaar number instead - the portal may offer this as an alternative.

steps.title: Read the status result
steps.description:
The status shows whether your application is active, in migration, approved for ₹3,000, or flagged for review. If the status shows 'removed' or 'ineligible', note the reason stated.

Common reasons: income taxpayer, government employee, invalid bank account, duplicate entry. Each reason has a specific remedy.

steps.title: If payment has not come despite 'approved' status
steps.description:
Check your bank's Aadhaar-linked DBT status at myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/bank-seeding-status. If the seeding is inactive or linked to a different bank than your current account, the payment will fail.

Update the Aadhaar-bank link at your bank branch before the next payment cycle.

extra_sections.title: During the Annapurna transition, do an e-KYC check
extra_sections.content:
The safest move right now is to confirm your Aadhaar bank seeding and complete any e-KYC.

Several women stayed on the old amount only because their Aadhaar link was pending when the revision came.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible for Annapurna Bhandar in 2026
content: The eligible population for Annapurna Bhandar is women aged 25 to 60 years who are permanent residents of West Bengal. The flat payment of ₹3,000 per month applies to all eligible women, with no distinction based on caste or category.
Income taxpayers are explicitly excluded. This means women from households where anyone files an income tax return are ineligible.

This is the most significant eligibility restriction that catches otherwise low-income families - a household where an adult child is salaried and files an ITR can make the mother ineligible for the scheme.

Permanent and retired government employees - from state government, central government, panchayats, statutory bodies, local bodies, and municipalities - are ineligible. Retired government employees who receive a regular pension are also excluded.
This includes both teaching and non-teaching staff in government-aided educational institutions.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 Who Is Eligible for Annapurna Bhandar in 2026 (more)
content: Women aged below 25 are not eligible. This is a change from the old Lakshmir Bhandar scheme which covered women from age 21.
Women who were receiving Lakshmir Bhandar and are now aged 22-24 were removed from the list during the migration audit. They will become eligible when they turn 25.

The upper age limit of 60 years means women above 60 are not covered by Annapurna Bhandar. However, women above 60 may be eligible for the Jai Johar scheme (for SC/ST elderly women) or Old Age Allowance programmes run by the state.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 Who Is Eligible for Annapurna Bhandar in 2026 (continued)
content: These are separate applications from Annapurna Bhandar.

Self-employed women, women working in the unorganised sector (domestic workers, agricultural labourers, daily wage workers), women with small businesses, and homemakers are all eligible as long as they are not income taxpayers and their family does not have a government job or pension.

There is no family income cap listed in the Annapurna Bhandar eligibility criteria - unlike some earlier versions of Lakshmir Bhandar which in some districts used income as an informal filter. The formal disqualifying conditions are the specific categories (income taxpayer, government employee, pensioner) rather than a general income ceiling.

The scheme does not distinguish between women who are widowed, separated, or in an intact marriage. A widow living alone, a woman separated from her husband, and a married woman all qualify on the same terms.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 Who Is Eligible for Annapurna Bhandar in 2026 (more 2)
content: The marital status does not affect eligibility - what matters is age, residence, and the absence of the disqualifying conditions (government employment, ITR filing). This is an important feature for women in difficult personal circumstances who may otherwise feel they need a male household head to access welfare schemes.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 Who Is Eligible for Annapurna Bhandar in 2026 (part 2)
content: One nuance on the government employee disqualification: the rule applies to permanent or retired employees. Contract workers, daily wage earners, and scheme-based workers (like ASHA workers, Anganwadi workers, mid-day meal workers) who work for government programmes but are not on a permanent salary roll are not automatically disqualified.
However, ASHA and Anganwadi workers should check with their BSK, as some districts applied the disqualification broadly during the audit.

Women in tribal areas and in hill districts (Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Alipurduar) who are covered by autonomous bodies rather than the main state government departments should check whether the Annapurna Bhandar covers them. Some tribal sub-plans and autonomous councils have parallel welfare schemes, and the relationship between those and Annapurna Bhandar should be confirmed locally.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 Who Is Eligible for Annapurna Bhandar in 2026 (more 3)
content: For Aadhaar-bank linking: the most reliable way to check is at myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/bank-seeding-status using your Aadhaar number and mobile OTP. The page shows which bank account your Aadhaar is currently mapped to for DBT purposes.
If the account shown is old, closed, or different from where you expect to receive the payment, visit your bank to update the Aadhaar-DBT mapping.

extra_sections.text:
Of the 2.2 crore Lakshmir Bhandar beneficiaries, approximately 30 lakh were removed during the June 2026 audit. That is roughly 1 in 7.

The most common reasons: government employee or pensioner in the household, income tax return filed by a family member, or age below 25. If you were removed and believe the reason is incorrect, the appeal window is open - but the burden is on the applicant to show the disqualifying condition does not apply.

extra_sections.heading: New Applications and What to Do If You Were Removed
content: New applicants - women who were never on Lakshmir Bhandar and are now applying fresh to Annapurna Bhandar - have a 90-day enrollment window from June 1, 2026 through August 25, 2026. After August 25, the application window may close or move to a different phase.
Apply before the deadline.

The application form is available for download from socialsecurity.wb.gov.in in Bengali, Hindi, and English. Physical forms are also available at Duare Sarkar camps, BSK centres, and gram panchayat offices.
Fill in the form, attach Aadhaar copy, bank passbook copy, and a passport-size photograph. Submit at your local gram panchayat (rural) or BSK centre (urban).

extra_sections.heading: 📄 New Applications and What to Do If You Were Removed (more)
content: For women who were on Lakshmir Bhandar but were removed during the audit: the first step is to check your status at socialsecurity.wb.gov.in to confirm the reason for removal. If the reason is government employment, and you are no longer employed or the employment entry is wrong, you need to provide a document proving current non-employment - a service termination letter, resignation acceptance, or a declaration from the employer.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 New Applications and What to Do If You Were Removed (continued)
content: If the removal reason was 'income taxpayer' but no one in your family files an ITR, the most likely cause is a database linking error - perhaps a family member with the same name filed an ITR, or a previous employer filed Form 16 that was counted. In this case, obtain a certificate from the IT department (or an income declaration) and submit it through the grievance redressal process.
For women aged 22-24 who were removed because of the raised age floor (25 years): you do not need to take any action now. When you turn 25, your eligibility resumes and you can apply fresh.
The system should recognise your previous Lakshmir Bhandar history, which may help with faster verification.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 New Applications and What to Do If You Were Removed (more 2)
content: Bank account updates are critical during this migration period. If your bank merged (as many regional banks did in recent years), your old IFSC code may be invalid.
Check your current IFSC with your bank and update it in the portal. Payments sent to invalid IFSC codes are returned and require re-initiation, which can delay your payment by a full month.

Duare Sarkar camps (the WB government's doorstep service camps) are the most accessible point to get help with Annapurna Bhandar applications, status queries, and grievances. These camps are held periodically at the block or ward level.
Check your local panchayat or municipality for the camp schedule in your area.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 New Applications and What to Do If You Were Removed (part 2)
content: For women who were never enrolled in Lakshmir Bhandar - because they missed the original enrollment windows or were not aware of the scheme - Annapurna Bhandar is a fresh opportunity. The 90-day enrollment window gives first-time applicants until August 25, 2026.
After this window, it is not clear whether the government will open another round of fresh applications. Applying before the deadline is strongly advisable.
Joint bank accounts are not accepted for Annapurna Bhandar DBT payments. The bank account must be in the sole name of the beneficiary woman.

If you only have a joint account with your husband or another family member, open a new solo account before applying. Many state bank branches have simplified processes for opening accounts under welfare schemes - ask specifically for a DBT-linked savings account.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 New Applications and What to Do If You Were Removed (more 3)
content: The ₹3,000 monthly payment is credited directly to the bank account with no conditions on how it is spent. There are no requirements to show receipts, attend training, or produce certificates of usage.

The scheme is a direct income support payment. This unconditional structure is deliberate - it ensures the money reaches the woman without creating barriers that many low-income families cannot overcome.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 New Applications and What to Do If You Were Removed (part 3)
content: If you receive both Annapurna Bhandar (₹3,000/month) and are also a Kanyashree K2 beneficiary or a Rupashree Prakalpa recipient, there is no conflict. These are separate schemes for different purposes - Annapurna Bhandar is an ongoing monthly payment for adult women; Kanyashree and Rupashree are one-time education and marriage grants.
Receiving one does not disqualify you from the others, as long as each scheme's individual eligibility conditions are met.
Grievance resolution for Annapurna Bhandar follows the same channel as Lakshmir Bhandar did. The district Social Welfare Officer is the primary grievance authority.

For payment-related issues, the District Programme Officer handles escalation. If you file a written grievance and receive no response within 30 days, the next escalation is the District Magistrate's office through the public grievance window.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 New Applications and What to Do If You Were Removed (more 4)
content: Some women have asked whether receiving Annapurna Bhandar affects their eligibility for central government schemes like PM Matru Vandana Yojana or Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima. The short answer is: no.

Annapurna Bhandar is a state-level income support scheme and is not counted as disqualifying income or benefit for any central government scheme that this guide is aware of. However, always confirm with the specific scheme's implementing office for the most current rules.

extra_sections.heading: 📄 New Applications and What to Do If You Were Removed (part 4)
content: Finally, on the question of whether the ₹3,000 will increase further: the new government has framed Annapurna Bhandar as an improved version of its predecessor, and there is political momentum behind women-targeted welfare transfers in West Bengal. Whether the amount is revised upward in subsequent state budgets is speculative.
For planning purposes, the current confirmed amount is ₹3,000 per month. Check socialsecurity.wb.gov.in for any official announcements.

faqs.question: What happened to Lakshmir Bhandar status check in 2026?
faqs.answer:
Lakshmir Bhandar was replaced by Annapurna Bhandar from June 2026. Status check still happens at the same portal - socialsecurity.wb.gov.in.

Go to Track Applicant Status, enter your mobile number, complete the CAPTCHA, and submit. The portal shows whether you have been migrated to Annapurna Bhandar (₹3,000/month), are under review, or were removed during the audit.

faqs.question: Is Lakshmir Bhandar still active or replaced?
faqs.answer:
Lakshmir Bhandar has been officially replaced by Annapurna Bhandar from June 1/3, 2026. The new scheme pays ₹3,000/month to all eligible women, compared to ₹1,500 (General) and ₹1,700 (SC/ST) under the old scheme.

Existing verified Lakshmir Bhandar beneficiaries were automatically migrated. New applicants must apply fresh before August 25, 2026.

faqs.question: My Lakshmir Bhandar payment stopped in June 2026. What do I do?
faqs.answer:
Check your status at socialsecurity.wb.gov.in to see the reason. Common reasons for removal: someone in your family is a government employee or pensioner, someone in your family files an income tax return, your age is below 25, or your Aadhaar-bank link is broken.

Based on the reason, gather the relevant document proving the condition does not apply and submit a grievance through the portal or at your local BSK or gram panchayat.

faqs.question: What is the new Annapurna Bhandar scheme eligibility?
faqs.answer:
Women aged 25 to 60 years who are permanent residents of West Bengal. Ineligible if: anyone in the household files an income tax return, the woman is a permanent or retired government employee or pensioner, or she works in a government-aided educational institution.

No category distinction - all eligible women receive ₹3,000/month.

faqs.question: How do I apply for Annapurna Bhandar if I was never on Lakshmir Bhandar?
faqs.answer:
Download the application form from socialsecurity.wb.gov.in or collect it from a BSK centre, gram panchayat office, or Duare Sarkar camp. Fill in the form, attach your Aadhaar, bank passbook, and a photograph.

Submit at your gram panchayat (rural) or BSK (urban) before August 25, 2026. This is the 90-day enrollment window for new applicants.

faqs.question: I was removed from Lakshmir Bhandar because of income tax but no one in my family files ITR. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
This is likely a database error - possibly a family member with the same name, or a former employer who filed Form 16 that was flagged. Collect an income declaration or certificate from the Income Tax department showing no ITR is filed for your family.

Submit this through the grievance section at socialsecurity.wb.gov.in or in person at the district women and child development office.

faqs.question: Does Annapurna Bhandar cover women above 60?
faqs.answer:
No. The upper age limit for Annapurna Bhandar is 60 years. Women above 60 may be eligible for other state welfare schemes - the Old Age Allowance scheme and, for SC/ST women, the Jai Johar scheme.

These are separate applications from Annapurna Bhandar.

faqs.question: Can a woman with a small business or self-employment income get Annapurna Bhandar?
faqs.answer:
Yes, as long as she is not an income taxpayer. Self-employed women, small traders, agricultural workers, and homemakers are eligible.

The key disqualifier is filing an income tax return - not having income itself. As long as the family's income is below the ITR filing threshold and no family member files a return, the woman can apply.
